regions.text: 偶然に對する形面上的驚異は運命に對する驚異の形を取ることがある。

quote.translation: Metaphysical wonder at the contingent sometimes takes the form of wonder at fate.

regions.text: 偶然が人間の實存性にとつて核心約全人格的意味を有つとき偶然は運命と呼ばれるのである。きうして選命としての偶然性は必然倒との異稲結合によって、「必然！偶然者」の構造を示し、超越的威力を以て嚴として人間の全存在性に臨むのである。ヘラクレイトスの運命（Elpappem），fatum）の觀念に於ても「必然ー偶然者」の構造が見られる。

quote.translation: When the contingent carries a core meaning for the existentiality of the human being, a meaning that engages the whole person, it is called fate, and contingency as fate, through its heterogeneous combination with necessity, displays the structure of "the necessary-contingent", confronting the whole existence of the human being sternly and with transcendent power.

quote.translation: Kant, in his Lectures on Metaphysics, holds that what is absurd among the connections of things is blind necessity (die blinde Notwendigkeit), that is, fate (Schicksal), and blind chance (das blinde Ungefähr), that is, chance (Zufall); the former, he says, is "what is founded neither on the essence of the matter nor on other causes", the latter "what is contingent in every respect" (Kant's Vorlesungen über die Metaphysik, 2 Aufl. hrsg. v. Schmidt, S. 52 f.).
